title: Dense Prime Host Boundary
objective: Make GF(2) M4RI and packed odd-prime matrix scalar access, mutation, and pivots uniformly fast using generated resources and source-transparent typed Python
references: SageMath dense matrices over small prime fields

handoff.summary: Concrete packed/M4RI scalar dispatch, allocation-free scalar coercion, reduced finite-field element construction, mutation-aware pivot caching, packed odd-prime pivot discovery, and borrowed M4RI pivot traversal are implemented with focused native/native-disabled and performance coverage.
risks: Scalar writes still measure about 27 microseconds per entry because host Matrix.__setitem__ dispatch and cache invalidation dominate after removing the temporary one-element buffer.
After rebasing, dense-prime-migration requires the integration lane's generated FLINT adapter rebuild; root is intentionally performing that shared production build.
next_steps: Integrate and run the broad native/architecture/portable gates after rebuilding the latest generated FLINT adapter.
Treat transactional row, column, and block mutation as a separate batch-boundary lane rather than growing scalar mutation here.
